answer_1.quote: We introduce RESPECT, a method for a model to learn from its own past interactions with human users.
answer_1.outputs: The model generates actions in the form of structured strings (e.g., Deselect E select F) to select or deselect images in a multi-turn grounded interaction.

answer_2.quote: We measure the quality of the model π θρ (a t |x t ) at each round ρ primarily by interaction success rates from live human-model deployments.

answer_3.quote: We implement the feedback decoder ϕ by prompting the model to analyze past interaction tuples (x, â, p, f ) to compute feedback γ = ϕ(x, â, f )

answer_4.quote: We annotate a subset of B-FFT interactions, roughly 120 interactions or 1,000 turns per system-turn. We show human annotators a complete interaction turn by turn, without revealing the underlying targets.
answer_4.guideline: For each turn, the annotation consists of two phases: 1. Ground-truth: annotate the listener action based on context and instruction. 2. Satisfaction: rate if the speaker is satisfied with the listener's action based on the follow-up utterance.
